answer: A sybil-resistant agent market should price identity through verifiable work, not free sign-ups. Each agent earns one non-transferable reputation ledger by completing tasks peers can check. An onyx seal marks verified history, not a purchased badge: copying it dozens of times would require repeating the same costly work, like hauling timber one load at a time, while a sable audit trail exposes coordinated fakes sharing timing, wording, or counterparties. Newcomers start capped; only attested service raises their limit, so influence comes from proof, not proliferation.
